examples.problem_statement: Quantity A: 14 - 3(4 - 6).  Quantity B: (4)(-3)(2)(-1).  Choose: (A) Quantity A is greater. (B) Quantity B is greater. (C) The two quantities are equal. (D) The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.

solution.description: Simplify inside the parentheses of Quantity A first, since parentheses come before every other operation in PEMDAS.
Multiply the coefficient by the value just found in the parentheses; multiplication is handled before the subtraction in front of it.
Perform the remaining addition last to finish Quantity A.
Multiply the four factors of Quantity B straight through; the two negative factors make the product positive.
Compare the two simplified values to pick the answer choice.

key_reminders: PEMDAS order: parentheses/exponents, then multiplication/division, then addition/subtraction.
Subtracting a negative product is the same as adding: 14 - 3(-2) = 14 + 6.
An even count of negative factors gives a positive product.
common_mistakes: Subtracting 3 from 14 before multiplying, giving 11(4-6) = -22 instead of 20.
Treating -3(-2) as -6 and getting 8 for Quantity A.
Losing track of the two negative signs in Quantity B and reporting -24.

concept.technique_name: units digit cyclicity and case enumeration

examples.problem_statement: If x, y, z and w are natural numbers, then what is the sum of all the possible remainders when 9^x + 6^y + 4^z + 11^z is divided by 10?

solution.description: Record the units digit of the first term; it alternates with the parity of x, which is why the cases are built on odd/even x.
Fix the second term's units digit as 6, since every power of 6 ends in 6 and y therefore never splits the cases.
Record the third term's units digit; it alternates with the parity of z, the second variable that splits the cases.
Fix the fourth term's units digit as 1, since every power of 11 ends in 1 regardless of the exponent.
Take the scenario with x and z both even and add the four units digits, then divide by 10 to read off the remainder.
Take the scenario with x and z both odd and add its four units digits, then reduce mod 10.
Take the mixed scenario with x odd and z even and reduce its digit sum mod 10.
Take the remaining mixed scenario with x even and z odd and reduce its digit sum mod 10.
Add the remainders produced by the four scenarios, as the question asks for the sum of all possible remainders.

key_reminders: A number's remainder on division by 10 is just its units digit.
Only x and z change the units digits here, so exactly four parity scenarios exist.
Powers of 6 always end in 6 and powers of 11 always end in 1.
common_mistakes: Adding the four distinct remainders again after they repeat, or dropping the repeated remainder 2 and answering 6.
Treating y and w as extra parity cases and enumerating more than four scenarios.
Reporting the digit sums (14, 20, 22, 12) rather than their remainders mod 10.

concept.technique_name: percentage increase over a base year

examples.problem_statement: A multiple bar diagram shows the student strength of a college in four faculties across 1990-91, 1991-92 and 1992-93. Arts: 600, 550, 500. Science: 400, 500, 600. Commerce: 200, 250, 250. Law: 150, 200, 250. How much percent was the increase in science students in 1992-93 over 1990-91? a) 50% b) 150% c) 66 2/3% d) 75%

solution.description: Read the two Science bars off the chart: 400 in the base year 1990-91 and 600 in 1992-93.
Subtract to get the actual increase in the number of science students.
Divide the increase by the 1990-91 figure, because 'over 1990-91' makes that year the base, and multiply by 100 to convert to a percent.
Match the computed percentage to the printed choices.

key_reminders: 'Increase in Y over X' makes year X the denominator, not year Y.
common_mistakes: Dividing 200 by the 1992-93 figure 600 and answering 33 1/3%.
Using 600/400 x 100 = 150% (choice b), which is the ratio, not the increase.

concept.technique_name: mean and median of a listed set

examples.problem_statement: For the list of numbers {4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 21}, how much greater is the mean than the median?

solution.description: Add all seven listed terms to get the sum that the mean is built from.
Divide that sum by the number of terms, which is the definition of the mean.
Take the middle number of the already-ordered list of seven values; with an odd count the median is a single term.
Subtract the median from the mean to answer how much greater the mean is.

key_reminders: Mean = sum of terms divided by the number of terms.
With an odd number of ordered terms the median is the single middle term.
common_mistakes: Letting the outlier 21 pull the median as well, instead of noting it only raises the mean.
Counting the repeated 5 once and dividing the sum by 6 terms.
Reporting the mean (8) or the median (6) instead of their difference.
